title: Solvent heterogeneity regulates assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Supramolecular polymers are fundamental mimics of biological assemblies with diverse functions. However, predicting monomer solubility and controlling the colloidal stability of the resulting assemblies in solution remain major challenges. As a result, their preparation commonly relies on solvent mixtures, which can generate local heterogeneities during sample processing—an effect that remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that solvent heterogeneity biases assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization, with the extent of this effect modulated by monomer structure. Using an amphiphilic Pd(II) complex as a model system, we uncover a thermally accelerated transition from kinetically controlled discrete nanostructures to thermodynamically stable supramolecular polymers in water/1,4-dioxane mixtures. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that this transformation is mediated by microscopic liquid–liquid phase separation within the mixed solvent, creating 1,4-dioxane-enriched microdomains with increased local monomer concentration. Thermal annealing enhances molecular mobility and promotes the growth and coalescence of these microdomains, facilitating the transition to one-dimensional fibers. Extending the investigation to structurally related monomers further identifies the metal center and hydrogen-bonding motifs as key design elements governing this behavior. By linking molecular design and solvent heterogeneity to pathway complexity, our findings highlight how mixed solvents can be used to control supramolecular polymerization.

title: Molecular architecture of Cryptococcus cell walls reveals species-specific chitosan-dependent remodeling
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are fungal pathogens that cause life-threatening infections, including cryptococcal meningitis. A distinctive feature of the cryptococcal cell wall is the extensive deacetylation of chitin to chitosan, a modification that is essential for virulence but whose structural role in cell-wall organization remains poorly understood. Here, we analyze the cell walls of wild-type strains of both species and their avirulent chitosan-deficient mutants, which serve as vaccine candidates. Loss of chitosan disrupted cell morphology and altered cell-wall ultrastructure, with more pronounced defects in C. neoformans. Solid-state NMR reveals that aggregated α-(1→3)-glucans form the principal rigid domain of the cell wall in both species and are closely associated with chitin microfibrils, whereas surrounding β-glucans and mannoproteins constitute a more dynamic matrix. Chitosan modulates hydration and flexibility, and its loss increases chitin exposure and triggers species-specific remodeling of the polysaccharide network. In C. neoformans, chitosan depletion increased α-(1→3)-glucan content and reduced β-glucan levels, whereas C. gattii selectively lost one α-(1→3)-glucan subtype while maintaining β-glucan levels. Although capsule production remained intact, chitosan deficiency altered glucuronoxylomannan linkage patterns and mannoprotein composition. These findings reveal how chitosan organizes cryptococcal cell-wall architecture and highlight distinct structural adaptation strategies among pathogenic Cryptococcus species.

title: Bacteroides–Escherichia interactions contribute to colonization resistance against Clostridioides difficile
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Commensal gut bacteria are key contributors to the resilience against pathogen invasion. This is exemplified by the success of faecal microbiota transplantation in treating recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection. Yet, characteristics of communities that can confer colonisation resistance and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. Here we use a synthetic community of 14 commensal gut bacteria to uncover inter-species interactions and metabolic pathways underpinning the emergent resilience against C. difficile invasion. We challenged this synthetic community as well as faecal-matter-derived communities with antibiotic treatment and C. difficile in a continuous flow bioreactor. Using generalised Lotka-Volterra and genome-scale metabolic modelling, we identified interactions between Escherichia coli and Bacteroides/Phocaeicola sp. as key to the pathogen’s suppression. Metabolomics and targeted validation experiments revealed that fructan-derived fructooligosaccharides, vitamin B3 biosynthesis, and competition for Stickland metabolism precursors causally contribute to suppression across multiple C. difficile strains and donor backgrounds. Analysis of metagenomics data from patient cohorts and clinical trials attested the in vivo relevance of the identified metabolic pathways and the ratio between Bacteroides and Escherichia in successful colonisation resistance. The latter was found to be a stronger discriminator than commonly used alpha diversity metrics. Together, our study uncovers emergent microbial interactions in pathogen resistance with implications for rational design of bacteriotherapies.

title: Accurately modeling long-term storage with minimum representative hours in large-scale renewable energy systems
abstract: Energy system optimization often relies on time series aggregation to ensure computational tractability. Aggregation generally loses the chronology of time steps, which renders the storage level representation challenging. Typically, this challenge is addressed by using representative days (RD) to utilize intra-day chronology, even though representative hours (RH) can describe the input time series more accurately at fewer representative time steps than RD. However, until now, the use of RH storage representation methods has been limited by either high computational complexity, poor accuracy in clustering and storage representation, or restricted applicability. Here, we present a novel storage representation method based on RH that combines the high accuracy of RH time series aggregation with the high computational efficiency of methods based on RD. Through benchmarking the four most established storage representation methods on a model of a net-zero European energy system, we find that the proposed method can reduce the solving time by over 95% for the same objective value compared to the most established RD and RH methods. The proposed method exhibits particular strengths at strong aggregations of around 100 to 500 representative hours per year, making the method especially applicable to large-scale and sector-coupled transition pathway models. The developed method for accurately modeling both short-term and long-term storage, along with the presented findings, is of practical relevance to energy system modelers who seek computational tractability in large-scale applications while avoiding the misallocation of storage and conversion capacities.

title: Revealing inter-cell water-gas-coupled transfer characteristics and degradation-driven evolution within large-scale fuel cell stacks
abstract: Hydrophobicity decay is a critical driving force behind the degradation of proton exchange membrane fuel cells. However, the cross-scale linkage between microscopic material-level hydrophobic degradation and macroscopic stack-level water-gas transfer behaviors remains largely obscure, as well as the further inducing consequences. Bridging the gap, this study reveals the inter-cell water-gas-coupled transfer characteristics and degradation-driven evolution within large-scale fuel cell stacks. Applying the micro-current excitation method on a 60-cell stack, the evolution of membrane electrode assembly (MEA) material states is recognized after the 1000-h durability test. Except for typical catalyst degradation, an anomalous degradation feature is captured, wherein hydrophobicity degradation facilitates internal water accumulation and reduces ohmic resistance, consequently leading to the performance rise in ohmic polarization region. The degradation inconsistency within stack is found to be correlated with flow maldistribution. At the inter-cell level, cells with lower flow rates suffer from more severe degradation due to water accumulation and potential air starvation, which is especially pronounced in end cells. At the intra-cell in-plane level, the hydrophobicity degradation of MEA at the air downstream region is also more serious. For stacks assembled with MEAs with different hydrophobic states driven by degradation, the internal water accumulation difference and inter-cell coupling effect combine to cause gas redistribution. The evolution of gas distribution with humidity clearly indicates that the tendency of water accumulation within degraded cells increases the flow resistance and decreases the flow rate under high humidity conditions. Consequently, degraded MEAs suffer a greater risk of water flooding and significant deterioration in dynamic response performance, which forms a vicious cycle of accelerated degradation. This study enriches the cross-scale degradation mechanism theory of fuel cell stacks and holds significant values for consistency guarantee and lifetime extension.

title: Maximising self-consumption in energy communities: a comparative study of demand flexibility and dynamic sharing strategies
abstract: Energy Communities (ECs) have emerged as a vehicle for actively engaging citizens in the energy transition, enabling them to generate, consume, store and share renewable energy. Maximising collective self-consumption is a key objective of ECs, as it allows members to better capture the benefits of shared energy generation, and several approaches have been developed toward this goal. However, most of existing works aim to maximise ECs’ self-consumption by applying demand side management strategies or increasing the benefits with dynamic energy sharing, but not combining them. This study is one of the first to propose a data-driven framework that leverages machine learning, optimisation, battery management and dynamic energy sharing strategies to increase the self-consumption of ECs. The impact of the optimisation and dynamic energy sharing coefficients on ECs’ self-consumption and electricity costs was examined, together with their combination. The application of the proposed framework to an established Renewable Energy Community (REC) in Spain shows that dynamic energy sharing yields better results compared to load optimisation, and their combination shows more promising results. Permitting more frequent updates of dynamic energy-sharing coefficients can improve the allocation of locally generated energy and support higher member-level self-consumption, particularly in communities with heterogeneous and seasonal demand profiles.

title: Machine Learning in Liquid Electrolyte Design for Rechargeable Batteries: Addressing Fundamental Challenges
abstract: ABSTRACT Designing high‐performance liquid electrolytes for rechargeable batteries requires simultaneously achieving fast ionic transport, a wide electrochemical window, and interphase stability, yet these objectives are intrinsically coupled and often involve competing trade‐offs. Electrolyte optimization remains a formidable challenge for conventional trial‐and‐error approaches. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) are transforming electrolyte research into a data‐driven and increasingly autonomous paradigm for accelerated materials discovery. This review provides a comprehensive perspective on how ML methodologies are tailored to address the fundamental challenges of liquid electrolyte design. We first introduce the physicochemical foundations of liquid electrolytes alongside key ML workflows, emphasizing dataset construction and feature representation tailored to electrolyte chemistry. We then examine ML strategies for predicting and optimizing ionic transport, electrochemical window, interphase regulation, and multi‐objective optimization, highlighting representative advances and practical design principles for rational electrolyte development. Finally, we discuss current challenges, including data quality, model generalizability, and interpretability, as well as future opportunities for developing mechanism‐informed and transferable ML frameworks. By bridging machine learning with electrolyte science, this review aims to facilitate the rational design of next‐generation liquid electrolytes and accelerate the development of high‐performance rechargeable batteries.

title: Synergy Between Controllable Sulfur Defect and NiS Cocatalyst Enabling Efficient Photoredox Coupling Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Semiconductor‐based photoredox coupling of selective oxidation of vanillyl alcohol (VOL) to vanillin (VAL) with H 2 evolution provides a sustainable alternative to conventional industrial VAL synthesis processes, yet its performance is often hindered by rapid charge recombination and insufficient active sites. Herein, we report a facile one‐pot hydrothermal strategy to construct NiS‐decorated Zn 3 In 2 S 6 (ZIS) nanoflowers with controllable sulfur vacancies (V S ) for efficient co‐production of VAL and H 2 . Moderate concentrations of V S regulate the surface electronic structure and act as oxidation active sites to optimize VOL adsorption. Meanwhile, uniformly dispersed NiS cocatalysts serve as efficient electron relays and reduction active sites, accelerating charge migration and promoting H 2 generation. Benefiting from the interfacial synergy between V S and NiS, the optimal 1%NiS‐ZIS‐V S2 catalyst delivers an 18‐fold enhancement in both VAL and H 2 production rates relative to pristine ZIS, together with excellent stability and broad substrate versatility. This work highlights the critical role of defect‐cocatalyst synergy in designing advanced cooperative photoredox catalysts for sustainable chemical synthesis.

title: Engineering Advanced Electrocatalysts for Energy‐Saving Zinc−Air Hybrid Batteries: Concurrent Energy Storage Coupled With Chemical Upgrading
abstract: ABSTRACT Additive‐assisted zinc−air hybrid batteries (ZAHBs) that couple favorable additive oxidation with oxygen reduction represent ideal energy storage candidates, distinguished by high theoretical energy density, reduced charging voltage, and functionality for electrochemical upgrading of organics or wastewater. Herein, a critical overview of ZAHBs is provided, commencing with the fundamental electrochemistry (including advantages, working mechanisms, cell configurations, and evaluation parameters) and the selection criteria for small‐molecule additives (including theoretical potential, solubility, stability, toxicity, and volatility). We then summarize recent progress in three categories of ZAHBs (i.e., wastewater‐purified, value‐added, and redox‐mediated), discussing alternative anodic oxidation reactions (e.g., alcohol, urea, hydrazine, and iodine oxidation) coupled with cathodic oxygen reduction, along with the underlying catalytic mechanisms. Particular emphasis is placed on catalyst design strategies spanning electronic (ligand engineering, heteroatom doping, electron delocalization, orbital hybridization, and built‐in electric field), geometric (defect engineering, curvature engineering, and nano‐confinement effect), and interfacial (high‐energy interface, heterostructure, interfacial microenvironment, and core–shell structure) modulations. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges and future perspectives for advancing ZAHBs. This review offers valuable guidance for the rational design and practical deployment of next‐generation energy devices.

title: Site‐Selectively Engineered MoS 2 /ReS 2 Heterostructures for High‐Performance Supercapacitors
abstract: ABSTRACT Layered MoS 2 holds great potential for supercapacitors; however, its intrinsically low electrical conductivity, sluggish electrochemical kinetics, and susceptibility to Mo dissolution severely hamper its electrochemical performance. Here, we propose a selective‐doping‐coupled heterostructure engineering strategy, in which atomic Fe preferentially incorporates into the MoS 2 domain, while the local structure of the ReS 2 component remains largely preserved, forming an Fe‐doped MoS 2 /ReS 2 (Fe‐MRS) heterostructure. Theoretical and experimental results reveal the formation of a built‐in electric field at the Fe‐MRS interface, driving electron transfer from ReS 2 to Fe‐doped MoS 2 , reconfiguring the Mo‐S electronic structure, while simultaneously strengthening Mo─S bonds and suppressing Mo dissolution. Moreover, Fe incorporation is energetically favored at octahedrally coordinated Mo sites within the MoS 2 domain, modulating the local electronic environment of the MoS 2 domain and thereby facilitating coupled electron/ion transport. Consequently, the Fe‐MRS electrode delivers high specific capacitance and excellent cycling stability with a capacitance retention of 97.0% over 5000 cycles. Moreover, asymmetric supercapacitors assembled with the Fe‐MRS anode achieve a high energy density of 55.2 Wh kg −1 at 1000 W kg −1 , maintaining good structural and mechanical robustness. This work offers clear guidance for leveraging selective doping to engineer heterostructures with enhanced electron‐ion coupling for advanced electrochemical energy storage systems.

title: Ligand Electronics and Metal‐Site Acidity Enable High‐Voltage MOF Electrolytes for Quasi‐Solid‐State Lithium‐Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐metal batteries (LMBs) coupled with Ni‐rich cathodes offer high energy density for next‐generation energy storage. Their practical implementation, however, is limited by electrolyte oxidation and interfacial degradation under high voltage. Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) would regulate ion solvation and stabilize electrode‐electrolyte interfaces in quasi‐solid‐state electrolytes, yet the molecular origins of their oxidation stability remain unclear. Here, we identify ligand electronics and metal‐site acidity as key descriptors for high‐voltage‐stable MOF electrolytes. Electron‐withdrawing ligands lower the HOMO energy levels of MOFs, while hard Lewis‐acidic Al sites further enhance oxidation resistance. Guided by this principle, we design a perfluorinated Al‐based MOF, Al‐FBDC, featuring a high oxidation onset potential of 4.82 V (vs. Li + /Li). Incorporating Al‐FBDC into a composite cathode reconstructs the local electrolyte environment at particle‐level interfaces, thereby suppressing parasitic reactions and cathode degradation under high‐voltage operation. As a result, Li||Al‐FBDC@NCM quasi‐solid‐state cells deliver excellent long‐term cycling stability and rate performance, retaining 82% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C over 3.0‐4.5 V, while maintaining robust performance even at 4.6 and 4.8 V cut‐off voltages and with controlled electrolyte loading. This work identifies a general design principle for high‐voltage‐stable MOF electrolytes and offers a practical route toward high‐energy‐density LMBs.

title: Covalently Locked Donor–Acceptor Block Copolymer Nanoparticles Enable Efficient, Stable and Reproducible Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic photocatalysts with tailored properties and unique processability offer a sustainable route to solar hydrogen. To maximize light harvesting and charge generation, donor and acceptor materials are usually physically mixed to form D:A heterojunction nanoparticles (NPs). However, weakly constrained interactions can promote phase segregation, morphological evolution, and limited reproducibility. Here, we introduce an all‐conjugated donor–acceptor block copolymer, PBDB‐T‐ b ‐PYT, in which covalent linkage between PBDB‐T and PYT segments constrains nanoscale donor–acceptor organization and promotes intramolecular charge transfer. Compared with nanoparticles prepared from a physical PBDB‐T:PYT blend, PBDB‐T‐ b ‐PYT nanoparticles exhibit stronger photoluminescence quenching, more persistent charge‐associated transient absorption features, and improved photoelectrochemical charge extraction. As a result, hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) rates exceeding 120 mmol cm −2 g −1 h −1 (>450 µmol h −1 ) are achieved with low Pt loading (b ‐PYT NPs retained 95% of the initial HER rate after 96 h of photocatalysis. Conversely, NPs prepared from physically mixed PBDB‐T and PYT show lower activity and faster deactivation, consistent with morphology‐driven losses. PBDB‐T‐ b ‐PYT also maintains high performance across polymer batches, improving reproducibility. These results establish all‐conjugated donor–acceptor block copolymers as a promising design strategy for combining high activity, operational stability, and reproducibility in organic nanoparticle photocatalysis.

title: High‐Energy and Long‐Life Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 2 F 3 Cathodes via Multielement V‐Site Modulation of Local M–O/F Bonding
abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries are promising for sustainable energy storage, but their energy density still lags behind lithium‐ion systems. Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 2 F 3 (NVPF) is an attractive high‐voltage polyanionic cathode, but fluorine loss generates low‐voltage Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 impurities that lower energy density and aggravate lattice deformation during cycling. Here, we report a multielement V‐site charge modulation strategy, realized in Na 3‐δ V 1.9 Zr 0.02 Ti 0.02 Cr 0.02 Fe 0.02 Al 0.02 (PO 4 ) 2 F 3 (ME‐NVPF). The deliberate combination of high‐valence Zr 4+ , Ti 4+ , and same‐valence Cr 3+ , Fe 3+ , Al 3+ cations creates a heterogeneous M–O/F bonding network with multi‐directional electrostatic interactions enhancing lattice‐F retention that completely eliminates NVP impurities, lowers the Na + migration barrier, and reduces unit‐cell volume variation to merely 2.87%. Consequently, ME‐NVPF delivers a record‐high energy density of 477 Wh kg −1 , sustains 11 000 cycles, operates across −40 to 80°C, and is further validated in 600 mAh‐level pouch cells. This work establishes multielement compositional regulation as an effective strategy for designing high‐energy, long‐life, and all‐temperature polyanionic cathodes.

title: Stress‐Resistant Plant Cell‐Wall Inspired Cell Armor Enables Red Blood Cell Lyophilization
abstract: ABSTRACT Lyophilization offers an attractive route for ambient‐temperature storage of biological systems by eliminating cold‐chain dependence and suppressing solution‐phase degradation. However, lyophilizing mammalian cells remains challenging due to their vulnerability to coupled stresses, including ice‐induced mechanical injury and membrane destabilization during freezing and dehydration. In nature, stress‐resistant plant cells survive extreme conditions through multifunctional cell walls. Inspired by their natural survival strategies, we engineer an artificial membrane armor (AMA) that enables efficient lyophilization of red blood cells (RBCs). This biomimetic AMA integrates a nanoporous zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF‐8) for mechanical support, a water‐retentive polymer matrix for hydration retention and colloidal stabilization, and Zn 2 + coordination preserves membrane fluidity and suppresses freeze‐ and dehydration‐driven membrane phase transitions.
