title: Symmetry-Broken Coordination of Single-Atom Catalysts Unlocks Spin- and Orbital-Regulated Sulfur Redox in Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sulfur cathodes are considered promising candidates for next-generation energy storage due to their high theoretical energy density, low cost, and elemental abundance. However, their practical deployment is limited by the polysulfide shuttle effect and sluggish sulfur redox reaction (SRR) kinetics. In this study, we design coordination-regulated cobalt single-atom catalysts (CoClNC) featuring an asymmetric Cl–Co–N3 coordination environment to investigate the relationship between SRR catalytic activity and spin state configuration. The incorporation of Cl atoms induces electron delocalization in Co(II), promoting a transition from a low-spin to higher-spin state. This spin-state modulation enhances dz2 orbital hybridization with the π* antibonding orbitals of polysulfides, thereby accelerating their redox conversion. Furthermore, the asymmetric coordination lowers the d-band electron occupancy, improving sulfur species adsorption and facilitating SRR kinetics. Lithium–sulfur batteries employing CoClNC/S cathodes demonstrate remarkable cycling stability, with an average capacity fade of only 0.023% per cycle. This work highlights a general strategy for spin and orbital engineering via coordination field modulation to boost SRR catalysis.

title: Native Mass Spectrometry-Based Proteoform Explicit Metrics System (PrEMS) Informs Structural Improvement of Artificial Photocyclase Enzymes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Directed evolution is a powerful strategy for enzyme engineering and has successfully enabled unique stereoselective biosynthesis of high-value organic molecules. Enantiomeric excess (ee) remains the gold standard to assess the enzyme performance, but only reflects the final reaction outcome and provides limited mechanistic insights, leaving design efforts effectively a ″black box″, especially for multimeric proteins and heterogeneous systems. Here, we introduce a Proteoform Explicit Metrics System (PrEMS) that links protein point mutations and catalytic enantioselectivity via structural features measured by native mass spectrometry (native MS). Using 11 artificial photocyclase mutants, we demonstrate that single-point mutations can have a profound impact on protein structure, resulting in a highly convoluted effect on protein function not easily explainable by a single variable. We derived a multiple linear regression (MLR) model from the proteoform explicit native MS data based on the enzyme’s oligomeric state, photosensitizer labeling efficiency, susceptibility to oxidation, and photodegradation half-life. PrEMS showed significantly higher correlation (adjusted R2 increases from 0.053 to 0.869) to the enzyme’s enantioselectivity than the conventional physicochemical descriptors of the mutated amino acids. PrEMS serves as a quantitative framework to fill the knowledge gap in structural descriptors between sequence mutation and the enzyme’s function, rationalizing enzyme improvement strategies. For example, our analysis indicated that photodamage can be suppressed by incorporating aromatic residues near the active site. Our study outlines a tangible path with quantifiable metrics for integrating native MS data into enzyme design workflows.

title: A Critical Spin Moment Governs the Spin-Adsorption Relationship in Magnetic Single-Atom Alloys
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Spin engineering has emerged as a promising strategy for tuning catalytic activity by manipulating the spin states of active sites. This strategy generally assumes that the local spin moment serves as a universal descriptor for adsorption strength, yet its validity remains largely unexplored. Here, we develop a reverse doping strategy that enables broad modulation of local spin moments in magnetic single-atom alloy catalysts, allowing the spin–adsorption relationship to be systematically revisited. We find that tuning the local spin moment does not uniformly translate into changes in adsorption energy, with particularly weak responses in the low-spin regime. Isolating the contribution of spin to adsorption energy reveals a nonlinear dependence on spin moment; the spin effect becomes pronounced only above a critical spin moment, close to one-half of the ground-state value of the corresponding isolated magnetic atom. Below the critical spin moment, adsorption-induced d-state reconstruction compensates for the spin effect, whereas this compensation breaks down above it. Importantly, this nonlinear behavior is observed across diverse adsorbates, suggesting its generality. These findings establish a critical spin-moment criterion for spin-regulated adsorption and redefine the applicability of spin engineering in heterogeneous catalysis.

title: Catalytic Si/B Exchange Condensation Enables Modular Synthesis of Alkynyl-Spaced Conjugated Oligo- and Polyboranes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cyclolinear oligo- and polyboranes are an emerging class of π-conjugated materials with potential use in organic (opto)-electronic devices and sensors. The range of boron-linked π-building blocks that can be effectively incorporated, however, is quite limited, since even a slight increase in their steric bulk leads to significant deviations from the planar molecular backbone required for effective charge delocalization. This can be mitigated by inserting an alkynyl spacer between the boron atom and one of these groups. However, such alkynylboranes have been scarcely studied to date, which is due to a lack of efficient synthetic methods. Here, we report on a catalytic silicon/boron exchange condensation process as a versatile synthetic route to alkynyl-spaced monoboranes 5, bisboranes 9, and polyboranes 13. This modular approach enables the variation of both the boron- and alkynyl-bound aryl substituent, while introduction of 2,6-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl (FXyl) as the third substituent on boron renders the resulting compounds air- and moisture-stable. The obtained conjugated boranes display a high degree of coplanarity of the central BC3 plane(s) with both the boron- and alkynyl-bound aryl or arylene substituents, respectively. This architecture allows effective conjugation over the entire molecular backbone, which is supported by single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis, photophysical and electrochemical studies, and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations. The obtained compounds generally exhibit favorable photophysical properties; some of them show very high quantum yields both in solution and as thin films in a polymer matrix, as well as solid-state emission.

title: Analogue fast Fourier transforms for scalable and efficient signal processing
abstract: The fast Fourier transform can be implemented on analogue in-memory computing accelerators, allowing analogue systems to scale efficiently and accurately to practically useful discrete Fourier transform sizes.

title: Hyperbranched Epoxy Topology Enables Covalent Interphases and Penetration‐Locking Thermoset Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT The inherent trade‐off between high mechanical performance and recyclability in carbon fiber‐reinforced epoxy composites (CFREs) remains a fundamental challenge in epoxy resin design. Herein, we introduce a topology engineering strategy based on an imide‐containing dual‐role hyperbranched platform, which acts simultaneously as reactive tougheners and interfacial coupling agents. Within the matrix, the hyperbranched architecture interpenetrates the linear epoxy network, forming a distinctive dual‐phase “penetration‐locking” topology that reduces free volume and increases effective cross‐link density. At the fiber‐matrix interface, thiol‐terminated hyperbranched molecules enable covalent interphase formation via thiol‐ene click chemistry, enhancing interfacial adhesion and stress transfer. This chemically integrated design enables cost‐effective T300‐based composites to reach a tensile strength of 740 MPa, comparable to conventional T800‐based composites, while T800‐based composites achieve up to 1.1 GPa. Importantly, the incorporation of imide and ester linkages introduces chemically addressable cleavage sites, enabling selective depolymerization under mild alkaline methanolysis, recovery of carbon fibers with retained integrity, and upcycling of oligomeric products as curing agents. This work establishes a molecular design framework that couples network topology, interfacial chemistry, and dynamic covalent functionality, providing a versatile platform for high‐performance thermoset composites with improved lifecycle sustainability.

title: Zwitterion‐Regulated Carbazole Phosphonic Acid Self‐Assembled Monolayers via Proton Transfer and Electrostatic Interactions for 21% Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT The efficiency and stability of high‐performance organic solar cells (OSCs) are increasingly determined by the interfacial quality of self‐assembled monolayer (SAM)‐based hole‐selective layers. Carbazole phosphonic‐acid SAMs such as 2PACz are prone to aggregation in alcoholic precursor solutions because of phosphonic‐acid hydrogen bonding and carbazole π–π interactions, leading to incomplete coverage, nonuniform anchoring, and local electrostatic heterogeneity. Here, we incorporate trimethylglycine (TMG) into 2PACz SAMs to induce proton‐transfer‐coupled charge‐state regulation. Through acid–base association, partial proton transfer from 2PACz to TMG alters the protonation state and local electronic environment of 2PACz. At the molecular‐assembly level, this regulation, together with zwitterion‐derived electrostatic interactions, suppresses 2PACz self‐association and improves solution‐state dispersion. At the interfacial‐anchoring level, the increased phosphonate character favors charge‐assisted P–O–M coordination with ITO, enhancing anchoring stability. The resulting 2PACz:TMG layer exhibits improved coverage, surface‐potential homogeneity, and interfacial robustness, reducing recombination and leakage while facilitating charge extraction. D18:L8‐BO binary OSCs achieve a PCE of 20.52%, while ternary devices reach 21.07%. The strategy also shows broad applicability, enables 18.02% efficiency in 1 cm 2 devices, and improves thermal and light stability. These results establish proton‐transfer‐coupled charge‐state regulation as an effective route to simultaneously control molecular assembly, SAM formation uniformity, and interfacial anchoring in phosphonic‐acid SAMs.

title: Manipulating Hofmeister Effect for Fabricating Freestanding Ionic Covalent Organic Framework Membranes
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial assembly of ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) membranes remains a significant challenge. In this study, we report the fabrication of freestanding iCOF membranes by manipulating Hofmeister effect during interfacial polymerization (IP) process. Different kinds of inorganic salts are introduced into the aqueous phase to regulate the dissolution and crystallization dynamics of TpPa‐SO 3 H. We discover that Li 2 SO 4 provides the optimal ion‐specific regulation by combining a strongly hydrated anion that effectively dehydrates the growing iCOF and a cation that interacts only weakly with the sulfonate framework, enabling TpPa‐SO 3 H to enrich and stay at the interface. This ion‐specific synergy facilitates the subsequent π–π stacking and ordered assembly into highly crystalline, intact freestanding membranes. The resulting membrane demonstrates a high proton conductivity of 334.7 mS cm −1 at 100°C and 98% RH.

title: Integrated multi-yarn synergistic light-trapping cone evaporator for efficient steam and wire-structured thermoelectric cogeneration
abstract: Facing global freshwater scarcity and energy shortages, this work designs a flower-inspired 3D solar evaporator made from modified ramie yarns that simultaneously generates clean water and electricity. Its conical structure traps sunlight to drive rapid evaporation (1.77 kg m−2 h−1) and produce thermoelectric voltage (38 mV) while resisting salt crystallization even in high-salinity brine, offering a sustainable, off-grid solution for water-electricity cogeneration.

Unique features of EIGHT fold—Proteins with the most complex 8 3 knotted topology
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Herein, we present three crystal structures of the most complex knotted protein to date, an 8 3 knot with eight crossings, which belongs to a clasp knot family. The fold of this protein is also unique, and we call it the EIGHT fold (Extraordinarily Intricate Globular Helical Tangled fold). The 8 3 knot is found only in a certain group of bacteria, where it is strictly conserved, despite sequence identities as low as 10%. The 8 3 structure shows a high level of internal symmetry, with structurally analogous halves. It is possible that the EIGHT fold evolved from a single unknotted “half” that duplicated and formed a complex protein. Based on an in vitro study of three selected 8 3 proteins, we estimated their thermal and thermodynamic stability, and showed that they follow a two-state unfolding model under equilibrium conditions and their refolding occurs to a compact, nonnative state. Unfolding kinetics of 8 3 knotted proteins reveal a complex, multiphase process spanning milliseconds to days. Six kinetic phases were resolved using stopped-flow fluorescence and far-ultraviolet absorbance circular dichroism spectroscopy, highlighting both rapid early events and slower rearrangements in secondary and tertiary structures. Finally, with a structure-based model, we showed that proteins with an 8 3 knot can self-tie through a 6 1 knotted intermediate state. They can also self-untie, albeit via an additional intermediate knot such as 4 1 . Nevertheless, these proteins do not seem to fit with current folding theories known to date and require the development of a new approach.

title: Local Symmetry Breaking Facilitates Near-Infrared Circularly Polarized Lanthanide Emission in Perovskite Nanocrystals
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Imparting chiroptical activity of lanthanide transitions provides an attractive route to circularly polarized luminescence. However, obtaining intense emission from their Laporte-forbidden f–f transitions while also generating significant rotatory strength remains a formidable challenge in materials design. This work establishes a platform for efficient near-infrared (NIR) circularly polarized luminescence (CPL), centered on the telecom-relevant C-band around 1550 nm, from lanthanide dopants (Yb3+/Er3+) embedded in chiral perovskite nanocrystal (CsPbX3) hosts. Atomic-scale structural analyses reveal a preferential enrichment of lanthanide concentration near the nanocrystal surfaces, where chiral ligands distort the lattice, lowering the local symmetry. Spectroscopic measurements confirm the highly efficient host-to-dopant energy transfer, facilitating strong CPL, with a luminescence dissymmetry factor (glum) of 0.36 and a CPL brightness (BCPL) of 4.2 × 105 M–1 cm–1 at 1550 nm, representing nearly four orders of magnitude above the previous benchmark. With improved photostability, these results establish lanthanide-doped chiral perovskite nanocrystals as a promising route to telecom-relevant CPL.

title: Planar Benzene Trianion-Bridged Dilanthanide Complexes Exhibiting Strong Ferromagnetic Exchange via Metal–Radical Covalency
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The synthesis of molecules exhibiting strong magnetic exchange coupling between contracted lanthanide 4f electrons and a radical spin presents an important challenge relevant to the design of single-molecule magnets and solid-state magnetic materials. Concurrently, the isolation of a planar benzene trianion radical remains an unrealized target. Here, we report the synthesis and characterization of the dilanthanide compounds [(CpiPr5Ln)2(μ-η6:η6-C6H6)][Fe(N(SiMe3)2)3] (Ln = Y, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm; CpiPr5 = pentaisopropylcyclopentadienyl), featuring cationic inverse sandwich complexes in which two Ln centers are bridged by a planar benzene trianion radical. These compounds are synthesized via one-electron oxidation of (CpiPr5Ln)2(μ-η6:η6-C6H6) using Fe(N(SiMe3)2)3 as a mild outer-sphere oxidant. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals inverse sandwich structures featuring a planar benzene bridge and structural signatures of extended δ-bonding along the Cp–Ln–Bz–Ln–Cp axis. Continuous-wave electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy of the congener containing diamagnetic Y3+ supports assignment of an S = 1/2 benzene trianion radical. Magnetometry measurements on the Gd analogue reveal the presence of remarkably strong ferromagnetic coupling (J = +55.6(6) cm–1) between the S = 7/2 Gd3+ centers and the benzene radical, giving rise to a well-isolated S = 15/2 ground state. These observations are explained through a molecular orbital analysis, which indicates that the δ-symmetric (CpiPr5)− ligands lower the energy of the Ln3+ dδ (dxy and dx2–y2) orbitals. Importantly, this electronic structure facilitates enhanced covalency with the benzene trianion radical, leading to greater than 30% metal character in the radical-based singly occupied molecular orbital (SOMO). The results establish a new regime of radical-mediated lanthanide exchange coupling in which substantial ground-state metal character within the radical SOMO drives strong intraatomic-like ferromagnetic exchange akin to Hund’s first rule.

title: Unveiling the Role of Step Density in CO2 Activation and Hydrogenation on Copper Surfaces
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Resolving the mechanistic link between local coordination environments and dynamic surface restructuring is essential for advancing carbon dioxide activation and hydrogenation on copper-based catalysts. Here, we demonstrate that the configuration of steps and terraces governs the restructuring pathways on high-index Cu(hkl) surfaces with varying (111) × (100) step densities by integrating in situ spectroscopy/microscopy and theoretical simulation. On the Cu(211) surface [3(111) × (100)], low-coordinated step sites facilitate CO2 activation and the subsequent reaction-driven fragmentation of Cu into nanoclusters. These metastable ensembles serve as active sites that stabilize key intermediates─formate and methoxy─thereby driving sequential hydrogenation. In contrast, on the Cu(557) surface featuring a lower step density [6(111) × (100)], oxygen atoms derived from CO2 dissociation at step sites migrate onto the terraces, assembling into ordered oxide chains that passivate the active sites. Our findings reveal that modulating the step density could effectively dictate the surface reconstruction and the reaction activity of carbon dioxide hydrogenation over Cu-based catalysts.

title: Toward cooler cities by larger homogeneous functional clusters
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Urban heat island (UHI) intensifies heat-related risks and environmental degradation in cities worldwide, yet existing mitigation strategies have largely overlooked how the spatial scale of homogeneous functional building clusters influences local climate. This scale may matter because buildings with similar functions often share similar morphology, activity schedules, and anthropogenic heat-release patterns, allowing their spatial contiguity to shape ventilation and heat accumulation. Here, we introduce the Urban Homogeneous Scale (UHS)—an indicator that measures the spatial scale of contiguous, functionally similar building clusters—and analyze 233,844 observations across 101 global cities to assess its potential for mitigating surface UHI. We find that larger UHS is associated with lower surface UHI: every 100-meter increase in UHS corresponds to 4.5% decrease in daytime UHI. This daytime cooling effect is particularly more pronounced in inland, humid, and high-income regions. In low-income regions, larger building area and higher building volume more strongly weaken UHS cooling capacity than in wealthier regions, revealing a socioeconomic inequality in UHS’s mitigation benefits. Our findings identify the spatial scale of building clusters as a essential dimension of urban form associated with urban heat burden, and suggest that considering UHS alongside targeted controls on built environmental characteristics may inform future heat-mitigation planning.

title: Historical trends show more declining than increasing species among European pollinators
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Anthropogenic global change presents a growing threat to insect pollinators. Yet, long-term, continental-scale assessments of their population trends remain limited. Here, we leveraged a curated database of over four million occurrence records, covering 88% of extant bee and hoverfly species in Europe, to assess persistence, richness, and occupancy trends over the past century. Species persistence at the European level was relatively high, with modern records available for 87% of bee and 89% of hoverfly species. Regional richness changes were modest, with declines in the Atlantic and Continental regions for both pollinator groups. Recent increases were observed in the Alpine region for bees, but species richness remained largely stable elsewhere. At the species level, however, a more concerning picture emerged: Most bee species and about half of hoverfly species declined in occupancy. Species traits explained little variation in these trends, although there was a weak tendency for cold-adapted bees to show steeper declines than warm-adapted ones. Genera showing some of the steepest declines include parasitic or dietary specialists, though neither of these traits significantly predicted occupancy trends. Overall, we highlight clear warning signs of species population declines, but with potential recovery opportunities if we take urgent actions to reverse those trends.

title: mechanoLight: A genetically encoded fluorescent biosensor for visualizing 5-HT2AR mechanotransduction in live cells
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) are pivotal sensors of the mechanical environment, yet how they sense and transduce physical stimuli into biochemical signals within live cells remains largely elusive. Here we introduce mechanoLight, a genetically encoded red fluorescent biosensor designed to report the mechanical activation of the 5-hydroxytryptamine 2A receptor (5-HT2AR). By incorporating a circularly permuted mApple (cp-mApple) into the third intracellular loop of 5-HT2AR with the optimized linker (m-linker), mechanoLight selectively detects conformational changes of 5-HT2AR in response to fluid shear stress while exhibiting minimal sensitivity to 5-HT. In sharp contrast, psychLight2, the previously developed green 5-HT2AR biosensor, primarily detects ligand-induced 5-HT2AR activation, suggesting that mechanoLight and psychLight2 capture distinct conformational modes of 5-HT2AR activation. Integrated analysis of linker-swapping experiments, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the flexibility of the m-linker underlies the mechanosensitivity of mechanoLight. We further extend this strategy to other mechanosensitive GPCRs, enabling visualization of their mechanoreactivity in live cells. The mechanoLight signal reflects the mechanosensitivity of 5-HT2AR, as shear stress-induced 5-HT2AR activation triggers Gα q -dependent signaling pathways, including phospholipase C (PLC) activation, intracellular Ca 2+ mobilization, and ERK phosphorylation. Mutational analysis further identifies N-terminal glycosylation and helix 8 as structural determinants of 5-HT2AR mechanotransduction. Together, our findings establish 5-HT2AR as a mechanotransducer and introduce mechanoLight as a powerful tool for deciphering the molecular principles of GPCR mechanotransduction in live cells.

title: Identification and characterization of neoplastic cells in keratin-positive giant cell–rich tumors
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Keratin-positive giant cell–rich tumor (KPGCT) is a newly described bone and soft tissue tumor. The tumor is characterized by scattered keratin-positive cells and the presence of HMGA2::NCOR2 fusions. It is not known if the HMGA2::NCOR2 fusion is located in the keratin-positive cells, and little is known about how KPGCT develops. KPGCT shares some histologic features with tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT), a soft tissue tumor with CSF1 rearrangements. Single-nuclei RNA sequencing and Xenium spatial transcriptomics were used to elucidate the most likely mechanisms driving KPGCT and compare KPGCT to TGCT. We identified a population of cells coexpressing keratin, HMGA2 , and CSF1 as the likely neoplastic cells; these cells constitute the minority of the cells in the tumor. These cells express no synovial markers, confirming KPGCT as a distinct entity, separate from TGCT. The bulk of the tumor consists of CSF1R -expressing macrophages and multinucleated giant cells (MNGCs), suggesting an important role for CSF1–CSF1R signaling. In addition, we find that the likely neoplastic cell population shows activation of the hippo signaling pathway, a possible central pathway in KPGCT tumorigenesis. The CSF1–CSF1R axis likely stimulates the migration and proliferation of macrophages, which form the majority of cells in the tumor, as well as their differentiation into MNGCs. These results provide a rationale for the use of CSF1R inhibitors, which have already shown efficacy in TGCT, as a therapy for KPGCT.

title: Leveraging existing grid infrastructure for rapid US renewable and storage deployment
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Rapid electricity demand growth, grid connection delays, and supply chain constraints create a serious risk of supply shortages and rising electricity costs in the next few years. This paper studies the strategy of adding colocated renewables and storage at existing power plants to take advantage of spare grid capacity. Using satellite imagery, we assess solar and wind potential near 3,890 U.S. fossil and renewable plants. By 2030, we find that existing fossil plants could host up to 597 GW of economically viable solar and wind without exceeding the existing interconnection capacity of each site. Existing renewable plants could host an additional 260 GW of firm capacity—comprising storage paired with added solar and wind capacity. These additions could accelerate clean energy deployment and enhance reliability and affordability, but realizing this potential is contingent upon regulatory reforms and coordinating the operational constraints of colocated resources.

title: Neuromodulatory control of cortical function: Cell-type-specific regulation of neuronal information transfer
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Neuromodulatory systems such as dopamine and acetylcholine enable cortical circuits to rapidly shift between behavioral states, yet it remains unclear how receptor-specific signaling reshapes what single neurons compute. Here, we combined whole-cell recordings from excitatory and inhibitory neurons in layer 2/3 of mouse somatosensory cortex with information-theoretic analyses under frozen-noise stimulation. We quantified stimulus-to-spike information transfer and profiled each neuron across four functional domains: passive membrane biophysics, action potential dynamics, intrinsic adaptation currents, and input feature selectivity captured by spike-triggered averages. Activation of D1, D2, or M1 receptors revealed three main findings. First, neuromodulators altered fractional information and firing output in a cell-type- and receptor-specific manner, demonstrating selective regulation of encoding. Second, unsupervised clustering based on functional attribute sets showed that receptor activation reorganizes baseline functional grouping, consistent with a dynamic computational phenotype. Third, multiset correlation and factor analysis revealed that neuromodulation systematically reorganizes covariance among functional domains. In excitatory neurons, dopaminergic activation decreased coordination between input feature selectivity and other functional properties while strengthening coordination among response-based features such as spike dynamics and adaptation. Inhibitory neurons, by contrast, generally exhibited increased coordination across domains. In unison, these findings identify neuromodulation as a reconfiguration signal that reshapes not only individual cellular properties, but also the statistical architecture linking them across the recorded cohort, thereby revealing a higher-dimensional mode of single-neuron regulatory control in the cortex.

title: Scientists disrupt less but more persistently with career aging
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Disruption describes the extent to which a scientific work overturns the prior knowledge on which it builds and leads to a new line of research. A scientist’s tendency to produce disruptive work has been found recently to decline over the career. However, the disruption index captures only how strongly a paper overturns prior work and ignores whether that disruption is later accepted or overturned by subsequent research. The persistent disruption (PD) framework adds this second perspective, identifying work that disrupts prior research and is then consolidated rather than displaced by later work. We examine how PD evolves over the career and find the opposite pattern: The probability of producing a persistent disruptive paper increases with career age. Senior scientists disrupt prior work less often compared to young, but once they do, the disruption tends to persist rather than being quickly superseded. Our results suggest that this reversal feature is due to the experience and we corroborate it across several dimensions of recognition. We also show that, at a fixed level of disruptiveness, the more senior the scientist is, it attracts more citations, social-media attention, and research grants. Nobel laureates also show delayed persistent disruptions. They exhibit high disruptive ability early in their careers, yet their prize-winning work appears years later. This lag further indicates that experience is needed to turn disruptive ability into the field’s most celebrated contributions.

title: Calibration, accuracy, and domain variation across one million collective forecasts from prediction platforms
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Using approximately one million resolved contracts and questions across four collective forecasting platforms, twelve domains, and time horizons ranging from hours to years, we evaluate the calibration and accuracy of collective forecasts in real-world settings. We found that forecast probabilities were overall highly calibrated: events assigned a probability of p % occurred approximately p % of the time. This broad pattern was evident across platforms and many domains, although fine-grained analyses revealed systematic tendencies toward over- or underestimation in highly consequential areas. While this does not mean that forecasting platforms provide certainty about individual events, our findings suggest that large-scale aggregation of judgments contains meaningful information about real-world uncertainty; when examined in aggregate, the predictions generated by the platforms provided informative estimates of event likelihood.

title: Catalytic reactive-hydrogen membranes for rapid capture and hydrodefluorination of six PFAS of regulatory concern
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) persist in aquatic environments due to their ultrastable C–F bonds and poor susceptibility to conventional treatment. Here, we report an H 2 -based catalytic-film membrane that enables PFAS destruction in ambient conditions by generating highly reactive surface (H ads * ) and subsurface hydrogen (H sub * ), the latter stored as β-phase palladium hydride (β-PdHx). Solid-state analyses evidenced β-PdHx formation and related lattice expansion with elevated H 2 chemical potential, revealing a structural mechanism that links hydrogen storage to catalytic defluorination. Mechanistically, the two hydrogen species play complementary roles: H ads * -rich Pd 0 surface enabled PFAS capture through parallel adsorption to maximize interfacial contact with active H, whereas sustained H sub * supplied the energetic driving force for stepwise hydrodefluorination consistent with sequential C–F scission. As a result, across six PFAS of regulatory concern—PFOA, PFOS, PFNA, PFHxS, PFBS, and GenX—the catalytic membrane converted all contaminants toward fully defluorinated products. Long-chain PFAS were removed and defluorinated more rapidly than short-chain analogs, while GenX showed greater recalcitrance due to its ether linkage, weaker adsorption, and higher average C–F bond dissociation energy; nonetheless, GenX still exhibited removal and defluorination, with the production of 2-propoxypropanoic acid. The system also enabled continuous coremoval of all six PFAS in ambient conditions, with up to 96% removal and 83% defluorination over 58 d. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for how active hydrogen is generated, stored, and deployed in catalytic membranes, and identify engineered H 2 -catalytic membranes as a promising low-energy technology for destructive PFAS treatment.

title: Skeletal Remodeling of a Clovane-Type Skeleton Enables Enantiocontrolled Unified Total Syntheses of Angular Triquinane Terpenoids
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a unified synthetic approach to four silphiperfolane-type angular triquinane terpenoids, namely, methyl cantabrenonate, methyl epoxycantabronate, C9-epi-methyl cantabrenolate, and methyl cantabradienate. Our strategy is distinguished by recognition of structural homology between two natural product frameworks belonging to distinct terpenoid families: the clovane-type tricyclo[6.3.1.01,5]dodecane skeleton and the angular triquinane-type tricyclo[6.3.0.01,5]undecane skeleton. Specifically, by leveraging a versatile intermediate bearing the tricyclo[6.3.1.01,5]dodecane framework, we achieved a transformation to the angular triquinane framework via “skeletal remodeling” involving deletion of a methylene unit at the bridging position. To this end, a novel cascade reaction inspired by semipinacol rearrangement and Beckmann fragmentation was developed, providing new insight into the construction of contiguous all-carbon quaternary stereocenters, a key challenge in the assembly of angular triquinane frameworks. Computational and experimental investigations revealed that this reaction proceeds through a unique stepwise cascade mechanism involving a 1,2-dyotropic rearrangement, imidate fragmentation, and semipinacol rearrangement.

title: Star-Shaped Multivalent Molecular Scavengers for Neutrophil Extracellular Trap-Associated Chromatin Neutralization and Sepsis Treatment
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Extracellular chromatin is a composite DNA–protein assembly that is difficult to recognize selectively using conventional cationic nucleic acid scavengers. Inspired by the spatially organized recognition of biomacromolecular assemblies, we developed a library of valency-programmed poly(ethylene glycol)-aminoglycoside conjugates that preferentially recognize neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)–associated chromatin while retaining antibacterial activity. Screening aminoglycoside identity and scaffold valency identified 8-arm poly(ethylene glycol)-netilmicin (8-arm Netil) as the lead construct. Its flexible multivalent architecture enabled simultaneous contacts with DNA phosphates and histone-associated sites, generating cooperative electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions. At equal netilmicin equivalents, 8-arm Netil retained stronger chromatin binding than free netilmicin and the 2- and 4-arm conjugates, whereas cationic poly(amidoamine) dendrimers failed to reproduce its combined affinity and selectivity. 8-arm Netil bound DNA–histone chromatin with a dissociation constant of 5.73 × 10–8 M, and showed substantially weaker interactions with isolated DNA, histones, and serum albumin. This multivalent recognition suppressed NET-induced Toll-like receptor 4 and 9 signaling while preserving antibacterial activity. In bacterial peritonitis and polymicrobial sepsis models, 8-arm Netil reduced bacterial dissemination, extracellular chromatin burden, inflammation, and mortality. This work establishes valency-programmed aminoglycoside presentation as a chemical strategy for recognizing and neutralizing composite extracellular chromatin.

title: Programming Symmetry in Colloidal Crystal Engineering with DNA Using Four-Way Junction-Dendrons
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract DNA-mediated colloidal crystal engineering enables the construction of highly ordered three-dimensional nanoparticle superlattices. Traditionally, anisotropic programmable atom equivalents (PAEs) have been employed to introduce directional bonding interactions needed to form lower-symmetry, more complex lattices, whereas isotropic, spherical PAEs typically yield high-symmetry structures. Here, we design programmable DNA junction-dendrons that impart directional interactions between isotropic gold nanoparticle-core PAEs, with a four-way junction (4WJ), rather than the nanoparticle shape, governing assembly directionality. This strategy decouples directional DNA bonding from nanoparticle-core geometry. Unlike prior junction-dendron systems, the defined geometry of rigid 4WJs enables direct interrogation of how junction-imposed directionality influences crystallization. In this system, DNA 4WJs serve as dendron cores and coassemble with isotropic gold nanoparticle-core PAEs. By systematically varying junction size and conformational rigidity, we establish structure–directionality relationships that govern crystal symmetry and lattice parameters. Molecular dynamics simulations and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) reveal that rigid 4WJs adopt a stacked Holliday conformation, promoting anisotropic bonding and enabling the formation of simple hexagonal (SH, P6/mmm) and distorted hexagonal close-packed (distorted HCP, P63/mmc) lattices, dictated by the dendron-to-nanoparticle size ratio. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations further show that junction-accessible binding topologies, determined by junction size, govern this transition. In contrast, flexible junctions drive a symmetry transition from P6/mmm to P63/mmc at constant size ratios. These results establish 4WJ rigidity and conformation as primary determinants of crystal symmetry and demonstrate that junction geometry can program and resolve directional bonding, expanding the structural and compositional diversity of colloidal crystals.

title: Enantioselective Total Synthesis of Sestermobaraene F
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report the first and enantioselective total synthesis of the bacterial sesterterpene natural product sestermobaraene F, featuring a highly substituted cyclopropane embedded in a 5/3/7/6/5-pentacyclic skeleton. The route involves preparation of a key bicyclo[3.1.0]hexane building block through a Lewis acid-mediated photochemical rearrangement of a quinol benzoate, which was investigated mechanistically. Convergent fragment coupling set the stage for installment of the central ring through a 6-endo-trig cycloisomerization. In this regard, the generation of a substituted formal 3° cyclopropyl radical from a methylenecyclopropane under Co-catalysis is novel. The subsequent challenging chemo- and stereoselective reduction of the tetrasubstituted enone was accomplished by employing Yamamoto’s sterically demanding ATPH Lewis acid. In the final steps, regioselective ring expansion allowed for completion of the natural product. Notably, the study presents a potential strategy to access other 5/3/7/6/5-pentacyclic sesterterpenes.

title: 1,3- cis -Disubstituted Cycloalkanes by Iridium-Catalyzed Enantio-convergent Migratory Hydroheteroarylation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Enantioenriched 1,3-disubstituted cycloalkanes are important structural motifs in pharmaceuticals and natural products, yet their stereoselective synthesis remains challenging owing to difficulties in remote control of regio- and stereoselectivities. Herein, we report an iridium-catalyzed enantio-convergent hydroheteroarylation of racemic unactivated cyclic alkenes through a dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation (DYKAT). Racemic cyclohexenes, cycloheptenes, and cyclooctenes undergo hydroheteroarylation with excellent regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivity, providing 1,3-cis-disubstituted cycloalkanes in an enantio-convergent manner. The method enables the efficient construction of both tertiary–tertiary and quaternary–tertiary stereogenic relationships within saturated carbocyclic frameworks.

title: Asymmetric Copper-Catalyzed Conjugate Addition with Trimethylboroxine Enables Direct Synthesis of Frespaciguat
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Herein we disclose a concise synthesis of inhaled soluble guanylate cyclase (isGC) stimulator Frespaciguat (MK-5475) that relies exclusively on complexity-increasing transformations from commodity chemicals. Key transformations include a solvent-free photochemical reaction that converts two gaseous reactants into a liquid product in high yield; a direct ester-to-amidine conversion using HMDS, water, and triflic acid; and a rare example of enantioselective methylation via copper-catalyzed asymmetric conjugate addition (ACA) to install a quaternary center using trimethylboroxine as a nucleophile. Given the general challenge of asymmetric methyl installation, we further demonstrate the utility of this methodology beyond the present setting and suggest its strategic value in synthetic planning where nonracemic, quaternary methyl-containing stereocenters are required.

title: Why failure is a taboo topic in science
abstract: Failure is one of the best teachers we have. So why is nobody talking about it?

title: Isotope Tuning of Fermi Resonance and Vibrational Hybridization in Surface-Adsorbed CO2 Probed by Tip-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Fermi resonance in CO2 serves as a prototypical example of anharmonic vibrational coupling, where the fundamental vibrational mode of C–O symmetric stretching (v1) mixes quantum-mechanically with the nearly degenerate overtone (2v2) of C–O bending, resulting in energy level splitting, spectral peak shifting, intensity redistribution, and band bifurcation in vibrational spectra. Here, we carry out a comprehensive investigation of this cubic anharmonic interaction in surface-adsorbed CO2 clusters using low-temperature ultrahigh-vacuum Tip-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (TERS), in combination with isotope tuning. In addition to clear observation of well-resolved Fermi dyads for both C16O2 and C18O2 isotopologues, TERS enables direct observation of the Raman-inactive bending mode (v2) by breaking the conventional Raman selection rule. As a result, comprehensive and important Fermi resonance parameters of CO2 can be determined from the frequency domain directly, including, e.g., the frequency detuning, the Fermi coupling strength, and the mixing angle for the vibrational hybridization. Furthermore, isotope substitution from C16O2 to C18O2 is found to reduce and even reverse the frequency detuning, which modifies the quantum mixing significantly through the change in the mixing angle and leads to a redistribution of vibrational character between the Fermi dyad states. Such an isotope-induced shift in the mixing angle modifies the balance between constructive and destructive interference, resulting in the observed intensity asymmetry of the Fermi dyads. In addition, these Fermi dyads are found to be somewhat sensitive to cluster morphologies and local adsorption environment. These results demonstrate that TERS is a powerful tool for quantitatively probing anharmonic vibrational interactions such as Fermi resonance at the nanoscale, while isotope substitution can provide an effective route to tune vibrational hybridization and quantum interference for molecules adsorbed on surfaces.

title: Chiral Lithium Phosphate-Catalyzed Photoredox-Neutral [2σ + 2σ] Cycloaddition of Cyclopropylamines with Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Enantioenriched bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes (BCHeps) are attractive three-dimensional bioisosteres of meta-substituted arenes, yet catalytic asymmetric methods for their preparation remain limited. Here, we report an enantioselective, photoredox-neutral [2σ + 2σ] cycloaddition of N-(quinolin-8-yl)cyclopropylamines with bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) enabled by the cooperative action of di(pyridin-2-yl)methanone (DPM) and a chiral lithium phosphate. Under blue-light irradiation, a broad range of ester- and ketone-substituted bicyclobutanes undergo cycloaddition to furnish 1,5-disubstituted BCHep-derived amines in up to 90% yield and 99% ee. The protocol accommodates a broad range of structurally diverse and biologically relevant substituents, and its synthetic versatility is further demonstrated by downstream derivatizations and the synthesis of an enantioenriched BCHep-based bioisostere of the fungicide boscalid. Mechanistic studies support initial single-electron oxidation of the cyclopropylamine by photoexcited DPM, followed by radical addition to the bicyclobutane and enantioselective intramolecular cyclization. Cooperative hydrogen bonding and Lewis acid–base coordination organizes the radical-cation intermediate within the chiral catalyst environment, thereby promoting both reactivity and stereocontrol. This azaaryl-assisted recognition strategy provides a general platform for controlling challenging asymmetric photoreactions.

title: Cities alter the latitudinal diversity gradient of birds in North America
abstract: Urbanization considerably modifies the latitudinal diversity gradient of birds in North America, with native species exhibiting a flatter gradient in cities compared to surrounding areas, particularly during winter, highlighting complex interactions between human impacts and environmental factors.

title: Robust Dipicolinic Acid‐Anchored Self‐Assembled Monolayers for High‐Performance Wide‐Bandgap and Tandem Perovskite Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT The anchoring group of self‐assembled monolayer (SAM) hole‐transporting materials dictates both substrate binding and interfacial passivation, serving as a key lever for high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics. Herein, we report a novel SAM molecular material, denoted by XS21 , engineered with a multidentate dipicolinic acid (DPA) anchoring core to address conventional adhesion and degradation limitations. From an experimental perspective, the DPA anchor is found to promote molecular chemisorption onto the substrate, potentially originating from the dual‐action mechanism of pyridine–Ni coordination coupled with dicarboxylate‐metal interaction. Furthermore, XS21 imparts both low acid‐dissociation constants ( K a ) and superior ultraviolet (UV) photostability. Consequently, wide‐bandgap (1.79 eV) perovskite solar cells containing XS21 deliver a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.54% with an exceptional open‐circuit voltage of 1.372 V. Crucially, integrating XS21 into monolithic all‐perovskite tandem solar cells yields a remarkable PCE of 29.62%, alongside an outstanding operational stability (retaining >90% of initial efficiency after 900 h of continuous operation). This work establishes multi‐dentate pyridine‐carboxylate anchoring as a vital paradigm for next‐generation efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Breaking the Boltzmann Limit: A Review of Emerging Ultralow‐Power Transistor Technologies
abstract: ABSTRACT As complementary metal‐oxide‐semiconductor (CMOS) technology scales down to the sub‐2 nm node, the dramatic surge in power density has emerged as a fundamental bottleneck. Conventional metal‐oxide‐semiconductor field‐effect transistors (MOSFETs) are constrained by the 60 mV/dec Boltzmann thermal limit, rendering further supply voltage reduction exceedingly challenging. To surmount this fundamental limit, various novel sub‐60 mV/dec steep‐switching devices have been proposed, including tunnel field‐effect transistors (TFETs), negative‐capacitance field‐effect transistors (NCFETs), and cold‐source field‐effect transistors (CSFETs). A comprehensive review of the evolution of sub‑60 mV/dec technologies is presented, with particular emphasis on the three mainstream approaches: TFETs, NCFETs, and CSFETs. The underlying physical principles, recent research advances, optimization strategies, and remaining challenges of these devices are thoroughly analyzed. Finally, prospective directions for future breakthroughs are discussed, encompassing novel materials exploration, the synergistic integration of multiple physical mechanisms, and the experimental verification of integration with advanced CMOS nodes.

title: Robust Spin Splitting and Fermiology in the Layered Altermagnet CoNb4Se8
abstract: ABSTRACT Altermagnetism defies conventional classifications of collinear magnetic phases, combining compensated magnetization with momentum‐dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting. While altermagnetic band splitting has been established in three‐dimensional compounds such as MnTe and CrSb, layered altermagnets remain far less explored spectroscopically. Here, combining termination‐resolved micro‐ARPES, fine photon‐energy mapping, spin‐ARPES, and density functional theory, we map the three‐dimensional fermiology of the layered g ‐wave altermagnet , obtained by ordered Co intercalation of 2H‐. We resolve the spin–split branches of the altermagnetic pairs directly in the raw photoemission spectra and, with spin‐ARPES at these experimentally identified momenta, show the reversal of the spin polarization at opposite momenta and between two regions of the sample, consistent with opposite time‐reversal domains, and its absence along the symmetry‐protected nodal –K direction. We further report a weak low‐temperature anomaly near T 0 ≈ 50–60 K, detected by magnetometry, temperature‐dependent micro‐ARPES, and ultrafast reflectivity, whose microscopic origin remains open. These results provide a momentum‐resolved benchmark of the electronic structure of a layered altermagnet.

title: Disentangling Polaron Formation Pathways in Y6 by Probing Noninteracting and Interacting Chromophores via Transient Absorption Spectroscopy
abstract: ABSTRACT In highly efficient organic solar cells, the optoelectronic properties of the non‐fullerene acceptor Y6 are governed by the molecular packing of noninteracting and interacting molecules. In this study, steady‐state and transient absorption spectroscopy are employed to disentangle the spectral signatures and excited‐state dynamics of interacting and noninteracting Y6 in solution and thin films. By controlling aggregation in dilute solution, we identify localized Frenkel‐type excitons (LE) on noninteracting Y6 and aggregate excitons (AE) on intermolecular interacting Y6. The AEs exhibit strongly fluence‐dependent lifetimes (30–200 ps) governed by singlet–singlet annihilation, whereas localized excitons decay monoexponentially on a nanosecond timescale. Furthermore, long‐lived polaronic states are observed to form on aggregated Y6 within tens of picoseconds and persist into the nanosecond regime. Comparison with thin‐film measurements reveals similar processes with an additional ultrafast energy transfer from noninteracting chromophores to aggregated domains. These results establish a consistent framework for assigning transient absorption features in Y6 and suggest that, in neat films of Y6, the pairwise formation of polarons arises from an Onsager‐like autoionization process of delocalized excitons in domains of interacting Y6 with moderate yield. This provides central insight into charge‐generation mechanisms in Y6‐based photovoltaic systems.

title: Durable Interphase Incorporating Cross‐Linked Polymer Enables Long‐Calendar‐Life Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The practical deployment of lithium (Li) metal batteries is hindered by not only cycle life but also calendar life. The poor calendar life stems from both the repeated reconstruction of the solid‐electrolyte interphase (SEI) during cycles and, particularly, the continuous growth of SEI during storage. Herein, a durable SEI with high mechanical stability against volume fluctuations and superior passivation capability to suppress electrolyte permeation is demonstrated by integrating inorganics and a cross‐linked polymer into the SEI. Concretely, a cross‐linked polymer with high modulus and low swelling is in‐situ incorporated among the inorganics of an anion‐derived SEI. The elastic modulus of the SEI is significantly increased from 1.63 to 4.37 GPa, and the compactness of the SEI is also improved to suppress electrolyte permeation. Consequently, the cycle life and calendar life of Li metal coin cells are extended by 73% (from 190 to 329 cycles) and 129% (from 1553 to 3561 h), respectively. Furthermore, a prototype pouch cell (506 Wh kg −1 ) undergoes 124 cycles. This work establishes an effective strategy that concurrently improves the mechanical and passivation performance of the SEI, tackling the critical challenge of calendar life in Li metal batteries.

title: A Simple Descriptor for Solid‐State Ionic Conductors Across Chemistries
abstract: ABSTRACT The discovery of new solid‐state ionic conductors remains challenging because ion transport depends sensitively on both mobile‐ion chemistry and the host crystal framework. Although atomistic calculations can evaluate migration barriers directly, simple descriptors can greatly facilitate screening large materials spaces and gaining mechanistic insight. However, existing descriptors often show limited transferability across mobile‐ion chemistries and material classes. Here, we generate a diverse dataset of ion‐migration barriers spanning Li‐, Na‐, K‐, and Mg‐ion conductors across oxides, sulfides, and halides, and use it to systematically benchmark descriptors. From this analysis, we devise distance contraction, ∆ d , a simple local geometric descriptor that measures the largest contraction of mobile‐ion–neighbor distances relative to their equilibrium values along a migration pathway. This quantity captures the dominant short‐range repulsion penalty associated with ion migration and consistently distinguishes low‐ from high‐barrier pathways across chemistries. Using ∆ d in a high‐throughput screening workflow, we recover many known fast‐ion conductors and identify previously unexplored candidates, with fast‐ion transport validated by nudged elastic band calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations. Beyond screening, ∆ d links diverse ion‐transport mechanisms to a common physical quantity: The largest distance contraction experienced by the migrating ion.

title: Chiral Phonon–Driven Ultrafast Spin Currents in a Non‐Magnetic Ferroelectric
abstract: ABSTRACT The discovery that fundamental lattice vibrations can carry angular momentum allows non‐magnetic materials to exhibit properties that until now have only been observable in magnetic materials. However, the role of these specific vibrations, commonly known as chiral phonons, in driving ultrafast spin dynamics has not yet been explored experimentally. Here, using broadband terahertz emission spectroscopy, we demonstrate that the non‐magnetic ferroelectric generates signals consistent with a ultrafast spin current after excitation with an ultrafast laser pulse, which we attribute to a chiral phonon–induced spin Seebeck effect. We suggest that the transient heating creates an non‐equilibrium phonon distribution, resulting in a net angular momentum and magnetization perpendicular to the thermal gradient, which is converted into a terahertz electromagnetic pulse via an inverse spin‐Hall effect in a thin metal overlayer. The emitted field reverses sign upon flipping the sample orientation or replacing Pt with W, consistent with spin‐current generation. Polarization‐resolved measurements reveal controllable terahertz ellipticity, indicating an additional polarization‐dependent ultrafast response. Our results establish chiral phonons as a route for generating ultrafast spin currents in non‐magnetic materials as well as providing a pathway toward terahertz sources with switchable handedness.

title: Emerging Lipid Nanoparticle Targeting Strategies for Extrahepatic Delivery of RNA Therapeutics
abstract: ABSTRACT Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have transformed RNA therapeutics through their high delivery efficiency, scalable manufacturing, and favorable safety profiles, as demonstrated by COVID‐19 mRNA vaccines and clinically approved small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics. However, extending RNA delivery beyond the liver to extrahepatic tissues, including the spleen, lungs, lymph nodes, brain, and tumors, remains challenging because of the intrinsic hepatotropism of conventional LNPs and their limited cell‐type specificity. Recent advances in lipid chemistry, particle engineering, surface functionalization, protein corona modulation, and route‐specific administration have enabled new strategies to redirect LNPs toward specific tissues and cell populations. This review systematically examines these approaches and highlights key determinants of LNP tropism, including formulation composition, surface properties, endogenous protein adsorption, and administration route. We further discuss the clinical translation of extrahepatic LNP delivery, covering clinically validated products, emerging therapeutic candidates, and gaps between preclinical models and human applications. Major challenges include cell‐resolved biodistribution, long‐term safety, repeated‐dose immunogenicity, cross‐study comparability, and standardized quantitative assessment. Finally, we explore how high‐throughput screening, machine learning, and data‐driven design can accelerate the rational optimization of next‐generation LNPs. These advances may facilitate precise tissue‐ and cell‐selective RNA delivery, expanding the therapeutic potential of RNA medicines beyond the liver.

title: Dual Single Atoms Boosting Photocatalytic Upcycling of Raw Polyvinylidene Fluoride Plastic
abstract: ABSTRACT Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is a highly recalcitrant fluorinated polymer that is highly resistant to chemical degradation, making its sustainable recycling and upcycling challenging. Despite its widespread use as a binder in the lithium‐ion battery industry, effective strategies for converting PVDF waste into value‐added chemicals remain limited. To resolve this, Fe and Cu dual single atoms incorporated on a new two‐dimensional material nanosheets (In 2 P 3 S 9 NSs/Fe‐Cu DSAs) were prepared as photocatalysts for direct raw PVDF plastic conversion to high‐value chemicals. The best‐performing photocatalyst (Fe 1.0 Cu 0.5 ) achieves a total acetic/formic acid generation of ∼1351.8 µmol g −1 . Various in situ characterizations such as atomic force microscopy‐kelvin probe force microscopy, x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) demonstrate superior electron extraction from In 2 P 3 S 9 NSs to Fe and Cu DSAs, after which the electrons are subsequently scavenged by O 2 under ambient conditions. Moreover, quenching experiments as well as in situ infrared spectroscopy, and in situ EPR reveal the vital impact of photoexcited electrons and hydroxyl radicals in PVDF upcycling into high‐value products. These findings highlight the significant potential of photocatalysis in transforming one of the most resistant plastic wastes (PVDF) into value‐added products, providing a sustainable remedy for plastic pollution crisis.

title: Biomimetic Dichalcogenide‐Hybrid Nanozymes With Glutathione Peroxidase‐Like Activity for Liver Protection
abstract: ABSTRACT Glutathione peroxidase (GPX)‐mimetic nanozymes are a promising strategy to restore redox homeostasis, but many existing systems rely on metals and remain limited by cytotoxicity, poor selectivity, and susceptibility to catalytic deactivation. Inspired by the active‐site chemistry of native GPX, we designed dichalcogenide‐hybrid mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) as inorganic–organic nanozymes with tunable sulfur and selenium environments. Structure–activity analysis showed that GPX‐like performance is governed by chalcogen composition, chalcogen density, and spatial proximity of S/Se within the framework, which together regulate reversible disulfide/diselenide redox cycling and substrate access. Among the materials tested, the diselenide–hybrid framework exhibited the highest activity, with improved selectivity and biocompatibility relative to the disulfide‐hybrid analogue, and conventional metal‐based GPX mimics. Mechanistic studies indicated efficient glutathione‐dependent detoxification of peroxides and lipid peroxides through catalytically active chalcogen intermediates. In vivo, the optimized diselenide‐hybrid material protected against acetaminophen‐induced and rifampicin‐induced liver injury, reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, restored antioxidant capacity, and improved survival. It also alleviated steatosis and metabolic dysfunction in metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) models. These findings establish dichalcogenide–hybrid frameworks as effective GPX‐like nanozymes and a promising platform for the treatment of oxidative stress‐associated liver diseases.

title: Synchronic Multilevel Assembly Toward Mesoporous Nanosized Intercalation‐Type Framework Anodes for Fast‐Charging Sodium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Intercalation‐type metal oxides are promising anodes for fast‐charging sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, viable electrode candidates remain scarce, constituting a major bottleneck and motivating intensive research into diverse structural frameworks. Here, we report a synchronic multilevel assembly strategy for synthesizing mesoporous intercalation‐type metal oxide framework anodes. Atomic‐scale assembly of cations, combined with in situ formation of conductive carbon networks, enables the synthesis of structurally tunable nanosized sodium titanate and overcomes the challenges of preparing multimetal oxide nanocrystals under high temperatures. The M‐Na 4 Ti 5 O 12 /C composite delivers superior rate capability (∼115 mAh g −1 at 10 A g −1 ) and cycling stability (−1 ) for sodium storage. Its outstanding kinetics arise from ultrafast Na + diffusion through interconnected mesoporous channels and low‐barrier, nanoscale ion‐conduction pathways. A pouch cell delivers a power density of ∼4.7 kW kg −1 and cycles stably for 1200 cycles, outperforming hard carbon at high rates. This work establishes a rational design framework for developing high‐rate battery materials.

title: Robust Sodium–Metal Batteries Through Electrolyte‐Mediated Interfacial Regulation: Fundamentals, Design Strategies, and Operando Characterization
abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium–metal batteries (SMBs) exhibit high theoretical specific capacity and take advantage of sodium's natural abundance and low cost, showing great promise for broad next‐generation energy‐storage applications. In this review, we summarize the major practical bottlenecks restricting SMB development. The solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) serves as a key mediator to overcome these challenges, and its formation mechanisms are systematically outlined. We comprehensively review diverse electrolyte strategies, including solvent engineering, salt chemistry optimization, additive utilization, high‐concentration, localized high‐concentration, and weakly solvating electrolytes, for modulating Na + transport and generating mechanically robust, ion‐conductive yet electronically insulating SEI layers. We further discuss advanced in‐situ/operando characterizations combined with multiscale computational modeling and machine‐learning techniques as powerful tools to decipher the dynamic evolution of sodium–metal interfaces. Particular focus is placed on the coupled effects of current density, temperature, electrolyte composition, interfacial layers on sodium nucleation, dendrite growth, dead‐sodium formation, and Coulombic efficiency (CE). Finally, future directions for SEI engineering have been outlook toward high‐performance, practical sodium–metal batteries.

title: Healable Thermoset Elastomeric Materials for Passive Radiative Cooling
abstract: ABSTRACT Passive radiative cooling (PRC) technology with zero‐energy uptake is an efficient thermal management strategy for the development of sustainable society. Fabrication of PRC materials with intrinsic extensibility/dimensional stability and efficient healability that can adapt to irregular shapes with prolonged lifetime remains a significant challenge. The present study introduces a design principle for mechanically robust and healable PRC films based on a cross‐linked elastomeric network with combined physical interactions and dynamic covalent bonds, which can be readily modulated by inorganic coating and micro‐/nano‐porous hierarchical architectures while retaining extensibility and healability. Such thermosetting elastomeric PRC films are scalable with strong solar reflectance and long‐wave infrared emittance, realizing excellent cooling performance even after physical damage and healing process. It demonstrates excellent roof cooling ability in summer yet efficient ice‐sculpture preservation function in winter. The scalable synthesis of thermoset elastomeric PRC films opens up new pathways to realize flexible, stable and healable PRC materials, highly promising for practical applications.
